answer:
Verdict: yes

## Priority inversion

Likely, over the whole trace (0–30,612 ms): **worker-2 (TID 628083, real-time priority 10)** waited on a futex associated with **flusher (TID 628085, priority 1)** in **509 waits**. During 83.3% of those waits, flusher was preempted; **compactor (TID 628086, priority 5)** held the CPU for all of that preempted time. So the medium-priority compactor appears to have held up worker-2 while worker-2 waited for the lower-priority flusher. Confidence is **medium**.

The trace supports this as a likely lock wait, but does not directly establish application-level lock ownership.
